native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB:
RESULT — PCA on the 12 forms of capital (capital.csv, 39 hundred-year bins, BCE 4300–500), 12 Z columns re-standardized, PC1 extracted with sign convention "ZMonument (monument count) loading positive".

METHOD/WORKFLOW (executed): loaded capital.csv with decimal=',' (German commas), dropped group/color; verified 0 missing values; re-standardized the 12 Z variables across the 39 rows; ran correlation-matrix PCA (NumPy SVD, n=39 × p=12); extracted PC1 scores per 100-year bin; characterized the two target phases (endpoints included); ran two robustness checks and a supplementary pollen comparison. Script: analysis_capital_pca.py; outputs: outputs/pc1_scores_by_century.csv, outputs/pc1_loadings.csv.

PC1 STRUCTURE (observed): PC1 explains 30.3% of variance (PC2 19.5%). With the stated sign convention, the POSITIVE pole is dominated by copper/gold (ZCU_AU +0.41), pottery decoration (Zkeverz +0.38), hoards/deposits (ZHort +0.34) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert +0.30); the NEGATIVE pole by pottery form (ZKeform −0.35), axes/celts (ZBeil −0.24) and amber (Zamber −0.24); monument count (+0.20) and monument size (+0.24) sit mildly positive. Across the full 4300–500 BCE series PC1 rises from ≈ −1.7/−2.0 (Early Neolithic) to ≈ +3.1 (OBA) and +1.8 (YBA) — i.e., PC1 broadly tracks long-term growth of metal-prestige/hoard-type capital.

PHASE CHARACTERIZATIONS (observed PCA results):
• Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, group MN): mean PC1 = −1.37 (sd 0.49), well below the full-series mean (0 by construction; full-series sd 1.91). Within-phase trend is NEGATIVE: OLS slope −0.26 per 100-y step, falling from −0.58 (3400 BCE) to −1.78 (3000 BCE), the phase minimum.
• Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, group SG): mean PC1 = −1.12 (sd 0.43), slightly higher than the Middle Neolithic (difference +0.26), still on the negative side. Within-phase trend is POSITIVE: slope +0.12 per 100-y step, rising from −1.50 (2900 BCE) to −0.41 (2300 BCE), the phase maximum.
• Phase ranking over all six groups (low→high PC1): EN (−1.74) < MN (−1.37) < YN/SG (−1.12) < LN (+0.33) < YBA (+1.85) < OBA (+3.09).

HYPOTHESIS (natural-language answer to the question): In a PCA of the twelve forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, the first principal component (~30% of variance) contrasts prestige-metal capital — copper/gold, hoards/deposits, and decorated pottery (plus, weakly, monument count/size) — against pottery form, axes/celts and amber. Both target phases lie on the negative (low) side of this axis. The Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) is characterized by the lowest and steadily declining PC1 of any post-EN phase (mean −1.37, falling from −0.58 to −1.78): low expression of metal-prestige, hoard and pottery-decoration capital combined with comparatively high pottery-form values. The Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) remains at a similarly low level (mean −1.12) but reverses the trend, with PC1 rising through the phase to −0.41 at 2300 BCE — the first sign of the recovery that accelerates through the Late Neolithic and peaks in the Older Bronze Age. Interpretation (distinct from the observed scores): the two Neolithic phases are thus jointly characterized by weak monetizable/prestige capital relative to the Bronze Age, with the Middle Neolithic marking a within-phase decline and the Younger Neolithic a modest, sustained upswing; supplementary pollen-openness data (Belau/Woserin) show nearly identical mean openness in both phases (MEAN −0.67 vs −0.66; 100-y smoothed −0.53 vs −0.57), consistent with no major openness-driven discontinuity between the phases — context only, not part of the PCA.

ROBUSTNESS NOTES (demoted per instruction): (1) Removing ZSichel (whose long run of exact zeros pre-2300 BCE could be structural) leaves PC1 essentially unchanged (EVR 32.6%; MN −1.44, YN −1.20; r = 0.996 with main PC1). (2) The raw century-point Z values in time_series_data.csv are numerically identical to capital.csv (all 12 variables, exact match), so using capital.csv vs. the time-series raw columns is equivalent; _inter columns simply interpolate between the same century points and were not needed.

LIMITATIONS: PC1 sign is arbitrary (convention stated above); re-standardizing the already Z-scaled columns is a modeling choice (results are near-identical without it, as the robustness check shows); ZSichel zeros may be absence-of-data rather than true zeros (checked, immaterial); 39 samples with piecewise-constant century values limit fine-grained trend inference; pollen PC1 is supplementary context only and does not enter the PCA.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (decimal=','), dropped group/color; re-standardized the 12 Z capital variables across 39 century rows (BCE 4300-500); PCA via SVD; PC1 sign oriented so ZMonument loading is positive; extracted per-bin PC1 scores; characterized MN (3400-3000) and YN/SG (2900-2300) by mean, within-phase slope and loadings; robustness: PCA without ZSichel and cross-check of raw century Z values against time_series_data.csv; supplementary pollen openness comparison (not in PCA).
